claims.text: Integrating CALPHAD modeling with high-temperature experiments enables accurate and efficient determination of melting temperature, fusion enthalpy and entropy, melting volume change, and liquid-phase thermodynamic properties across the high-entropy-alloy family.
Equimolar (La,Sm,Dy,Er,Nd)2O3 is an example of a single-phase, homogeneous high-entropy material.
Refractory high-entropy alloys with simple solid-solution structures and minor secondary phases are suitable initial materials for the proposed approach.
CALPHAD modeling over the full compositional range can capture non-ideal mixing in both solid and liquid phases.
Rare-earth high-entropy oxides undergo reversible phase transitions in the approximate range 1900–2400 °C.
The proposed measurements are performed under equilibrium conditions during controlled heating and cooling.
Most successfully prepared single-phase high-entropy compositions satisfy an atomic-radius-difference limit of about 15% associated with Hume-Rothery or Goldschmidt criteria.
Synchrotron X-ray diffraction can monitor polymorphic phase transformations and associated unit-cell volume changes in multicomponent rare-earth sesquioxides.
Non-ideal mixing in both the solid and melt phases mediates the observed thermodynamic responses.
Non-ideal mixing in a multicomponent high-entropy system shifts phase-transition temperatures.
Non-ideal mixing alters enthalpy, entropy, and other thermodynamic properties of fusion.
The cited high-temperature experimental techniques directly measure transformation behavior and volume changes.
The cited experiments establish that volume change specifically at melting can be measured accurately by in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction.
CALPHAD can extrapolate thermodynamic properties across composition and temperature spaces while representing solid- and liquid-phase stability.
The CALPHAD treatment used here explicitly accounts for configurational-entropy contributions across high-entropy-alloy composition spaces.
The melting point of equimolar (La,Sm,Dy,Er,Nd)2O3 is 2456 ± 12 °C.
The combined approach will generally determine melting temperatures across diverse high-entropy systems with uncertainties on the order of ±12 °C.
The combined approach will yield reproducible, quantitatively accurate fusion enthalpy, fusion entropy, melting volume change, and liquid-phase properties across diverse high-entropy systems.
Using only direct high-temperature measurements or only independent CALPHAD modeling is less accurate or substantially more resource-intensive than the integrated approach.
Accuracy is expected to deteriorate in systems with severe kinetic limitations or very high compositional complexity.

contradictions.description: The initial materials are described as both single-phase and homogeneous and as potentially containing minor secondary phases.

The intervention proposes modeling over the full compositional range, whereas the boundary restricts applicability to compositions satisfying atomic-radius criteria and excludes or questions very high compositional complexity.
